question: Ferrous sulphate on heating gives a solid product and two different gases. Select the gases evolved during the reaction.
solution:
The correct answer is** __Sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **chemical formula **of ferrous sulphate is FeSO₄.
 
• The strong heating of ferrous sulfate leads to the formation of a **brown solid (ferric oxide)** and 2 gases.
 
• This type of reaction is known as** decomposition reaction.**
 
• The **balanced chemical equatio**n of this reaction is:
 
 
• 2 FeSO₄ (s) → Fe₂O₃ (s) + SO₂ (g) + SO₃ (g)
 
 

Thus, the two gases formed are **Sulphur dioxide **(SO₂)** and Sulphur trioxide** (SO₃).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxygen:**

 
 
• Oxygen can be evolved through electrolysis of water, thermal decomposition of various oxides and oxygenic photosynthesis.
 
 
• Electrolysis: 2 H₂O → 2 H₂ + O₂
 
 
 
 
 
• **Disulphur: **
 
 
• Disulphur is evolved when an atmosphere of COS is irradiated with UV light.
 
• It can also be produced when S₂Cl₂, H₂S₂, CS₂, or C₂H₄S, PSF₃ or COS are irradiated.
 
 
 
• **Sulphur trioxide:**
 
 
• Sulphur trioxide is a chemical compound with the formula SO₃.
 
• Sulfur dioxide in air directly oxidizes to Sulphur trioxide extremely slowly:
 
 
• SO₂ + 1 over 2O₂ → SO₃
